title: S3 workspace producer ownership, generations, and lifecycle fencing

scope.phase: S3 producer ownership, execution generations, repository fencing, driver control, and recovery
scope.designAuthority: Candidate S3 design defines the accepted scope; this oracle pins observable behavior and does not require a particular module layout.
permittedBehavior: Additive transactional schema 5 to 6 migration and lifecycle records for provisional owners, revisions, operations, drivers, and narrow cancellation requests
Durable ownership and recovery intent before every covered workspace, Git, process, plan, review, check, integration, deliverable, restart, resume, and landing side effect
Explicit provisional planning ownership before plan acceptance, followed only by accepted-plan-gated generation creation
Distinct generations, immutable plan revision chains, globally unique attempt identity, generation-scoped projections, pinned roots, and truthful reconciliation
Repository-scoped cross-process exclusion, durable detached-driver handoff, bounded cancellation request channel, and read-only queries while a driver owns the mutation fence
excludedBehavior: Changing the configured default worktree root or activating nested-root default selection
Implicit adoption or rebinding of legacy runs/artifacts from path strings, graph IDs, branch names, or configuration
Cleanup, worktree pruning, artifact deletion, force removal, delivery receipts, cleanup eligibility, or retention expiry
Direct cancellation by killing a persisted PID outside the active driver's verified owned process tree
Committing, pushing, publishing a PR, merging, releasing, or claiming cross-platform support without execution evidence

preconditions: A representative canonical v5 DB contains all legacy runs, events, attempts, evidence, feedback, quota and S2 lifecycle rows, including unresolved legacy ownership.
Capture schema/data snapshots and database native identity.
cases.action: Migrate once to v6, close and reopen through current code.
expected: Migration is additive and transactional; all legacy columns, rows and payloads remain value-for-value unchanged.
Legacy generation/revision bindings remain NULL; no graph, path or branch inference occurs.
New lifecycle tables and constraints match canonical v6; reopening is idempotent.
noSideEffects: No deletion, rewrite, implicit generation, adoption, Git change, or external file mutation.
failureInvariants: Any unpreservable row or schema mismatch refuses without partial v6 state.

preconditions: A v5 fixture has sentinels in every legacy table; deterministic failure can be injected after actual v6 DDL begins.
A separate DB has a version newer than 6 and sentinel schema/data objects.
cases.action: Inject migration failure, then separately attempt to open the future-version DB through current S3 adapter.
expected: Injected failure leaves a valid v5 schema and exact prior data snapshot.
Current adapter refuses the unsupported future schema before writes; schema, rows, identity and journal mode remain unchanged.
noSideEffects: No destructive downgrade, partial migration, data rewrite, or replacement DB.
failureInvariants: This portable test does not substitute for execution of the external retained v5 binary case.

preconditions: Exercise the complete existing graph_id_is_legal grammar: every nonempty ASCII string containing only alphanumeric, dot, underscore and hyphen, including literal ".", "..", dotted IDs, and a long legal ID; lifecycle IDs remain separately opaque/generated.
Two generations of one graph contain overlapping task IDs and create separate attempts.
cases.action: Roundtrip accepted graph identities through persistence and selectors, then create path/ref records using generated lifecycle IDs; separately validate relative paths.
expected: Every previously legal graph ID, including ".", "..", and long IDs, roundtrips byte-for-byte as an opaque logical identity; no max-length narrowing or normalization is introduced.

Graph strings are never physical path/ref components: physical names use opaque generated lifecycle IDs. RelativePath rejects absolute/drive/backslash paths, empty components, dot/dotdot components and escapes, while preserving valid contained forward-slash-separated relative paths.
Distinct attempts have globally distinct AttemptIds even when task and graph repeat across generations; generation, graph, task, artifact and attempt identities remain non-conflated.
noSideEffects: Only values outside the existing graph_id_is_legal grammar refuse before side effects; legal graph ID "." and ".." remain accepted as logical IDs without path traversal.
failureInvariants: No logical-ID validation narrowing, dot stripping, normalization collision, physical path/ref traversal, max-length cap, or ID reuse.

preconditions: A new planning request is not yet reviewed or accepted; exercise plan success, retry, decline and failure.
cases.action: Start planning, inspect durable records, then separately accept and decline candidate plans.
expected: Every planning attempt has unique provisional ownership and durable output provenance before dispatch or writes.
No GenerationRecord, accepted hash, or executable attempt exists before explicit PlanAccepted.
Acceptance creates an immutable plan revision and generation pinned to that exact content; rejection retains discoverable provisional history.
Public cancellation of pre-graph planning targets an opaque provisional driver ID; status/inspect expose that active provisional driver without inventing a graph ID or generation.
noSideEffects: Concurrent planners never reset or share a scratch workspace; failure to persist provisional ownership prevents planner dispatch.
Cancellation does not require or fabricate a graph ID before a plan exists.
failureInvariants: No provisional artifact is mislabeled accepted; no empty/fabricated accepted hash.

preconditions: Instrument actual public plan, stage/start, accept/first tick, attempt, repair/check, node integration, deliverable build, landing, restart, resume, review and derived cache entry points with observable fake ports.
Pre-review start/review remains provisional and does not create the execution integration artifact.
cases.action: Invoke each producer and record event order at storage, filesystem, Git, process, planner, and review-output boundaries.
expected: Each covered effect has a durable typed owner and pending operation intent committed before first use.
Intent records exact graph/generation/revision/attempt/root/target identity applicable to that producer.
Integration creation is deferred until PlanAccepted and actual generation creation at accept/first tick. No integration worktree/ref is created pre-review.
noSideEffects: Missing LifecycleAccess or intent persistence failure causes zero workspace/Git/process/output mutation.
failureInvariants: No unregistered artifact, shared planning scratch reset, fabricated acceptance, or success recorded before observed effect.
Pre-review integration must not be created even if it could be provisionally owned; the resolved S3 design defers it.

preconditions: A faulting lifecycle writer can reject each producer's reservation or completion write.
cases.action: Inject reservation failure and completion-write failure around representative Git creation, process dispatch, check, review output and landing operations.
expected: Reservation failure prevents all corresponding external effects and returns the original error.
Completion failure leaves the committed operation pending/blocked, returns failure, and allows later reconciliation.
noSideEffects: No error is swallowed; no duplicate operation is launched to mask failed completion persistence.
failureInvariants: Durable success is never reported without post-effect observation and completion record.

preconditions: Accepted graph has generation N, plan revision chain, attempts, events, evidence, artifacts, branches and pinned root; include dirt in old integration artifact.
cases.action: Perform two successive explicit restarts; separately attempt restart while unaccepted and after out-of-band plan JSON/hash mutation.
expected: Each successful restart creates a distinct generation pinned to the current explicitly accepted revision/hash and same root alias/layout.
Every prior generation, event, attempt, evidence, artifact, branch and required object reference remains queryable and unchanged.
Changed/unaccepted plan refuses before side effects; ADR0028 mutation requires the designed revision authorization and does not rewrite generation's initial accepted hash.
noSideEffects: No worktree/ref deletion, reset_graph_execution, implicit cancellation, cleanup, or history rewrite.
failureInvariants: A restart cannot silently select a predecessor generation or move a run after configuration-root change.

preconditions: One graph has at least two generations with overlapping task IDs, different terminal/live states, revisions, attempts and evidence.
cases.action: Query active and explicit historical status, replay, attempts, review selection, export metadata and summary.
expected: Default operational queries resolve active generation once per command and only select its events, attempts, evidence, revision and Git metadata.
Explicit historical query returns the requested generation; aggregate summary labels generations rather than concatenating state folds.
Old and new generation projections cannot overwrite or mask one another.
noSideEffects: Queries do not mutate generation, initialize repository identity, or adopt legacy history.
failureInvariants: Graph ID alone is never a sufficient query scope for generation-specific state.

preconditions: An accepted plan revision has canonical JSON/hash, review authorization and linked generation; perform append and prepend mutations with require_review on and off.
cases.action: Mutate plan, review/accept as applicable, dispatch attempt, then tamper with stored JSON/hash out of band.
expected: Every mutation appends an immutable revision with predecessor, exact JSON/hash and truthful authorization; no prior snapshot is overwritten.
require_review=true blocks execution until reviewed; require_review=false follows ADR0028's explicit inherited mutation authorization.
Attempts/events reference exact revision; each generation's initial accepted hash remains immutable; out-of-band mismatch refuses before dispatch.
noSideEffects: Mutation does not synthesize a new execution generation or erase rejected/review history.
failureInvariants: No forged human approval, lost revision link, or silent hash pinning.

preconditions: Deterministic injected crash checkpoints cover after intent commit, before Git create, after Git create/before registration, after spawn/before child identity persistence, after observed effect/before completion, and during event transaction.
cases.action: Reopen store and invoke reconciliation for each checkpoint with fresh Git/process observations.
expected: No-effect intent may resume only after proving no producer can still act; observed expected effect finalizes idempotently; ambiguous partial state blocks with retained reason and intent.
No second dispatch or repeated non-idempotent Git operation occurs while outcome is unknown.
noSideEffects: No automatic cleanup, guessed owner, or history deletion during reconciliation.
failureInvariants: Fault checkpoints are injected and reported as such; they are not represented as actual power-loss tests.

preconditions: A multi-step pending operation has expected before/after refs, path identity and registration; alter each observed component between intent and continuation.
cases.action: Resume an operation after unexpected ref OID, missing/replaced worktree, alias/root identity mismatch, or unclassifiable process state.
expected: Operation transitions to visible blocked state with stable reason; all later steps stop.
Reconciliation revalidates exact repository, root, target and process facts before any continuation.
noSideEffects: No broad retry, force Git operation, path-based adoption, or cleanup is attempted.
failureInvariants: Unknown or drifted state never maps to success, dead, or safe-to-retry by default.

preconditions: One explicitly bound run pins root alias/path; config later selects a different root. A separate migrated run remains unresolved legacy ownership with events/attempts/evidence and Git fixtures.
cases.action: Run active producers after config drift and attempt resume/restart/accept/review/mutate/integrate on legacy run.
expected: Bound run resolves only its original pinned root; no default/config change relocates it.
Legacy reads remain available; every mutation refuses with LegacyOwnershipUnresolved and actionable identity guidance.
noSideEffects: Legacy refusal and reader opens preserve DB rows, files, refs, registry and do not initialize/bind/adopt identity.
failureInvariants: No inference from path, branch, graph name or configuration; explicit adoption remains S8.

preconditions: Use independent OS processes and deterministic barriers. A holds same-repository lifecycle mutation fence while B uses another checkout/config; test same authoritative DB, alternate/copy/replaced DB, and C using another repository.
cases.action: Race start/resume/restart/integrate/mutate across A and B, kill A at a barrier, then let B perform fresh identity and pending-intent reconciliation.
expected: A and B never both own writes; B receives bounded LifecycleBusy while A owns fence.
Alternate/copy/replaced DB cannot fork ledger authority; other repository remains independent.
After owner exit, next writer revalidates identity and pending intent before mutation.
noSideEffects: No spin loop, lock-file-exists heuristic, independent ledger creation, or stale-owner takeover.
failureInvariants: This is an actual spawned-process race, not a thread mutex test; report host OS and run count.

preconditions: Persist PID plus OS creation token and owned process-tree facts; fixtures include actual live child, actual terminated child, PID/image mismatch/reuse, access denied and ended_at with surviving descendant.
cases.action: Resume/cancel/dispatch against each state using actual process observations where available and injected unknown/ambiguous identity results separately.
expected: Live blocks conflicting mutation; confirmed dead allows only designed reconciliation; ambiguous or unsupported identity blocks and surfaces the reason.
Ended attempt alone does not imply process tree death; descendant liveness is respected.
noSideEffects: No PID/image-only downgrade and no duplicate worker dispatch.
failureInvariants: Label native process observations versus injected inaccessible/unknown cases; OS-specific support claims require that OS run.

preconditions: A owns active driver and worker; another process has only narrow control client. Requests cover exact repo/graph/generation/driver/task and all-task selectors, duplicate, stale, wrong-driver, wrong-generation and queue-cap boundary.
For pre-graph planning, the separate provisional-driver case uses typed provisional target; execution task selectors are valid only for generation targets.
cases.action: Queue cancellation while owner is active; exercise 64 outstanding-request cap, duplicate idempotence, stale successor protection, and cancellation with failed kill/uncertain tree.
expected: Control client performs only bounded cancellation-request INSERT; maximum 64 outstanding per driver; no arbitrary payload; provisional-driver and execution-generation targets are distinct types, and task selector is execution-only.
Owner acknowledges Applied only after killing its verified owned tree and observing termination; otherwise status is Pending, Blocked, Stale or OwnerLost with reason.
Default acknowledgement wait is bounded to 5 seconds; if owner has not completed by then, CLI returns honest Pending with request ID and current observable status.
noSideEffects: No direct PID kill, run/event/attempt mutation, lease acquisition, registry read, binding, root registration or adoption through request client.
failureInvariants: Cancellation request acceptance is not cancellation completion; bounded acknowledgement timeout reports current status honestly.
No active cancellation request may be directed to a stale provisional driver, successor generation, or wrong target kind.

preconditions: A blocking check and planner use deterministic controllable child processes; owner retains repository fence while polling.
cases.action: Queue cancellation during each blocking operation and observe owner ControlProbe/heartbeat cadence and process-tree termination.
expected: Owner checks requests at a target cadence of at most 100ms through existing 20ms loops and mandatory ControlProbe, except while a bounded Git operation is executing; use deterministic probe/tick evidence, not a 100ms wall-clock scheduling assertion.

Cancellation is exercised against actual controllable planner/check child processes; owner observes request, terminates only its owned tree, then commits the legal event/ended_at/ack. The default CLI acknowledgement wait is 5 seconds and returns Pending when exceeded.
Unrelated child process remains alive.
noSideEffects: No owner fence release before observed child termination; Git operations remain bounded and report finish/failure before consuming cancellation.
failureInvariants: Use barriers/monotonic deadline rather than timing sleeps; test cadence budget explicitly without claiming instant interruption.
Do not count a synthetic token-only unit test as actual public planner/check cancellation.

preconditions: Independent parent and detached child processes; inject crash before spawn, after spawn before PID/token persistence, before child lease acquisition, and before ready acknowledgement.
cases.action: Perform detach handoff with exact driver nonce; query control state during gap and after each injected crash.
expected: Pending handoff claim prevents another driver from stealing; child must acquire same authority, validate nonce/target, persist process creation identity and acknowledge ready.
Missing acknowledgement returns bounded pending/failed status; crash before identity is persisted remains ambiguous/blocked, not assumed absent.
noSideEffects: No hidden child or second driver runs without durable identity and lease.
failureInvariants: Use actual child processes; each crash window is separately labeled injected and leaves observable durable state.

preconditions: Active writer holds lifecycle lease and Windows registry handle; use read-only API session and separate CLI process.
cases.action: Read status, inspect, watch, and doctor while another process owns the lease; snapshot registry/database before and after.
expected: Read-only calls succeed or return bounded read-consistent results without acquiring writer lease; they do not initialize repository or root binding.
Cancellation request path validates actual common-dir and ledger identity without reading the exclusively locked registry.
noSideEffects: No WAL initialization, schema migration, registry write, root registration, adoption or lifecycle mutation from reads.
failureInvariants: Where OS does not support exclusive registry sharing, distinguish lock failure from product liveness behavior and report platform limits.

preconditions: Launch actual owner CLI with long-running fixture worker, second cancel CLI, and third status/inspect CLI as independent processes.
cases.action: Verify second mutator returns LifecycleBusy, status/inspect remains available, cancel queues exact request, owner acknowledges only after observed owned-tree death.
expected: CLI output exposes Pending then Applied or a truthful Blocked/OwnerLost status and request ID.
Third-party unrelated process remains alive; second mutator cannot fail/cancel the owner's worker.
noSideEffects: No persisted-PID kill bypass or mutation from read-only CLI.
failureInvariants: This end-to-end test is separate from adapter lease tests and from fake ControlProbe unit tests.

preconditions: Prepare one deliverable build with dirty/untracked output and branch, then prepare a second build; prepare landing with before/after ref snapshots.
cases.action: Rebuild deliverable and inject landing/merge failure before completion, after Git effect and after observation before journal completion.
expected: Every build receives a fresh immutable artifact/path/ref; prior dirty/untracked build and branch remain intact and queryable.
Landing operation records exact source artifact/head and destination before/after OIDs; ambiguous post-effect state blocks instead of repeating merge.
noSideEffects: No `remove_dir_all`, worktree prune, branch deletion, delivery receipt, cleanup eligibility or S4 claim.
failureInvariants: Drift stops remaining steps; successful operation does not claim delivery completion.
Wrong/stale provisional driver and execution-generation/task selectors do not cancel the planner.
expected: Cancellation request targets the typed provisional driver, not graph/generation/task.
Owner observes request within target polling cadence and terminates only its owned planner tree; it records outcome and retains provisional owner/output provenance.
If acknowledgement has not completed within five seconds, cancel returns Pending truthfully with request ID.
noSideEffects: No fabricated graph/generation ID, registry adoption, direct PID kill, unrelated child termination, or plan acceptance.
cases.action: Invoke public cancel --driver <opaqueid> from a separate CLI process; poll through bounded acknowledgement and inspect retained provisional state.
preconditions: Launch actual planning CLI before a graph ID exists and hold a controllable planner child active.
Status/inspect expose the opaque provisional driver ID.

cases.action: Create a v6 database with sentinel schema, rows, native identity and journal mode; invoke the actual retained schema-5 meshloop CLI against that database through a command that opens its store.

fixture.provisioning: Ignored external artifact must be provisioned from manifest on each host/CI; missing or mismatched fixture is a hard failure, never a skip.

expected: The actual older CLI process refuses the v6 schema with a nonzero exit and a bounded compatibility error.
The v6 schema/data snapshot, database native identity and journal mode remain unchanged after the process exits.
preconditions: Test is marked ignored with reason requiring retained exact schema-5 executable; acceptance collector explicitly runs this case with --ignored.
Resolve external binary path and expected SHA-256 from environment variables and verify both against the ignored manifest before launch.
failureInvariants: Missing executable, missing SHA, manifest/environment mismatch, wrong executable hash, or failure to exercise a real CLI store-open path fails the test. It must not skip, silently ignore, or count the portable adapter test as a substitute.
Observed counts must be one executed, one passed, zero ignored in the explicit --ignored run.
noSideEffects: No writes, WAL/journal-mode change, migration, replacement DB, deletion or registry mutation.
Read-only open never creates/migrates/initializes state; explicit migration is the only allowed write and only changes additive schema as covered by migration case.
cases.action: Read the absent location; attempt read-only open of pre-v6 DB; then explicitly run the writer migration to v6 and repeat legacy read.
preconditions: An absent database/root location is addressed through status/inspect/watch read-only composition.
A canonical v5 database has sentinel rows and unresolved legacy ownership; capture schema, rows, database native identity, journal mode, and filesystem entries.
failureInvariants: Do not let a successful migration test substitute for no-write refusal on the read path; do not silently migrate on read or discard legacy read visibility.
expected: Absent DB returns no managed runs and creates no directories, DB, WAL/SHM, registry or other files.
Pre-v6 read returns bounded SchemaUpgradeRequired before any write or journal-mode transition; all schema/data/identity/filesystem snapshots remain unchanged.
After explicit writer migration to v6, legacy run/history remains readable while unresolved ownership stays unbound and no adoption or repository/root binding is created.

requiredExecutedTestCount.criterion: Each named case must execute one or more non-ignored tests; required group filters must meet their nonzero minimums. The external retained-schema5 case is separately executed with --ignored and must report one pass and zero ignored. This oracle freezes expected behavior and makes no execution claim.

platformEvidence.networkFilesystem: no support claim from injected lock failures

validation.externalFixtureProvisioning: Provision the exact manifest binary and SHA on every acceptance host/CI; the current manifest is Windows .exe evidence only. No current CI coverage is claimed.
